cover.prompt: Huge Venus filling the lower two-thirds of the frame, thick swirling yellow clouds in sharp detail, a glowing sunlit edge curving across, a small fiery Sun peeking from behind its rim on the right, calm empty deep-black space across the top, photoreal, wide shot

fact_check.weak: Easy to absorb on one listen: 'सूरज का पूरा चक्कर' is ambiguous (it means Venus's orbit), and 'इसीलिए' wrongly links the unknown cause to the conclusion

hook_score.why: Short, a direct 'why' with the shock in it, and it matches the story's core question. The 'day longer than year' fact is fairly well known, so it's not a rare hook.
hook_score.was: शुक्र पर दिन साल से लंबा, और सूरज पश्चिम से?

why.3: A world map is shown on a screen in the corner. The planet looks like Jupiter, not Venus.
why.4: A person sits at monitors in front of the sun. This doesn't show Venus taking 225 days to orbit the sun.
why.5: Maps are on the wall and desk, and one is a US map. The Venus sphere looks odd sitting on the clouds.
why.6: Screens and panels are in the foreground. The rock hitting a planet is unclear.
why.7: A signboard or screen stands in the clouds. It has panels with text, and it doesn't show thick air slowing the planet.
